patch.value: Prevent served CLI fixture leases expiring during concurrent npm test

The unchanged installed served-forge CLI fixture in test/served-forge.test.ts acquires a 60000 ms publication lease and reuses it for a final push after many real CLI processes. A full Node-only npm test run failed with lease_expired after 86 seconds; the same test passed in both serial release gates (49 and 27 seconds) and in a focused Node-only rerun. Keep production expiry checks and explicit short-lease refusal tests intact; make this non-expiry fixture renew at publication or use a lifetime covering its execution budget.

Default concurrent npm test remains reliable under host contention without bypassing production lease expiry enforcement; Retain real installed CLI and HTTP coverage and explicit expiry refusal regressions

value.text: Evidence: the initial full default-concurrency Node-only npm test had 1549 passed, 1 failed, 4 expected Bun skips; installed served-forge CLI failed its final push with lease_expired after 86.364 seconds. This test and its lease fixture are unchanged from main. It passed in both serial release gates (48.649 and 27.070 seconds), a focused Node-only rerun (1/1), and the unchanged full Node-only retry (57.810 seconds; 1550 passed, 0 failed, 4 Bun skips). No production lease check, test assertion, timeout or fixture lifetime was changed. Keep this follow-up open for deterministic fixture renewal or lifetime handling under contention.
